_comment: Maps each Drive subfolder name to a report type and the parser module that handles it. Add entries as new report parsers are built. Subfolders without a parser are ignored (logged) until one is added. Rent Roll and Residential AR Analytics now have parsers (parse_rent_roll, parse_delinquency); both expose parse(path) and tie out against the report's own total rows. Weekly Leasing Reports is still pending and trade-out data is hand-entered in the workbook's Lease Detail tab. name_patterns is what lets the pipeline find a report that was filed into the wrong folder: fetch_drive first does its normal folder pass, then sweeps the drop tree (including _Unsorted) for unclaimed files matching these, case-insensitively. Folder organisation is unchanged and still what the Gmail filer maintains -- it is simply no longer the only way a report can be identified. An entry with no name_patterns stays strictly folder-bound.

subfolders._comment: The EliseAI weekly funnel parses from here too, so it works wherever the gmail filing lands it. The pending entry below is for this folder's intended content -- the RealPage rate tracker -- which has never yet arrived. The glob is anchored with a leading * because the Gmail-to-Drive filing prefixes the arrival date: '2026-08-25 leasing_funnel_report_2026-08-25.xlsx'. fnmatch matches the whole name, so a pattern starting at 'leasing_' silently skipped every prefixed file.

Same report type as Residential AR Analytics -- the PM files delinquency summaries in both. A file present in both folders parses twice and the second store overwrites the first with identical content, which is harmless.
Leading * for the same reason as the Weekly Leasing Reports entry: filed copies carry a 'YYYY-MM-DD ' prefix.
The building-metrics CSV. No parse/accumulate step -- update.yml runs populate_building_metrics.py on the newest one after the scorecard fill, passing Drive's landed_at as the arrival time.

The Yardi Unit Directory: every unit's floorplan, square footage, bedrooms and baths, for all properties in one export. Routed by the property-code rows inside it and tied out against each section's own Total row. Lives in the REFERENCE tree (GDRIVE_REFERENCE_FOLDER_ID), not the Gmail filer's drop folder: Building Info is the owner's hand-curated library of keys and long-lived documents, and the unit directory is exactly that -- the buildings' fixed description, not a periodic report. The glob leads with * because the filer prefixes the arrival date; fnmatch tests the whole filename, so an anchored pattern would skip every automatically filed copy.

The Landing 2025 Renewal Tracker and the 'Renewals since ...' extracts. Feeds the analyst workbook's Source Renewal Tracker grey tab, which is refreshed by pasting -- until a parser exists these are filed and logged, not read.
Weekly 'Prospect and applicant Report' extracts, one per leasing week.
Per-property daily/weekly leasing reports -- 'Daily Report- Week Ending ...', and the Madelon and Chorus daily reports. One family, several naming styles.

The 'Daily Tracker' workbook. Distinct from the daily leasing reports above -- different report, consistently ~157KB against their ~55KB -- so it gets its own folder rather than being merged on the strength of a similar name.
